name: Cheekbone makeup contour/highlight
lead: Cheekbone contouring and highlighting is a makeup technique in which darker shades are applied beneath the cheekbone and lighter or shimmering shades on top, intended to create the visual impression of more defined or higher cheekbones through shading.

The technique is discussed in style-focused parts of appearance communities as a non-surgical, reversible way to change perceived facial structure. No clinical studies on the effect were found, and the technique is a cosmetic styling practice rather than a medical treatment.

paras: The practice relies on optical effects: shadow tends to recede and highlight tends to advance, so placement along the hollow below the cheekbone and on the bone itself can alter how the cheek appears in photographs and in person. Application differs by product type, such as powders, creams and sticks.

The apparent shape of the cheek reflects both the skeleton and soft tissue. Anatomical literature describes the midcheek as formed from lid-cheek, malar and nasolabial segments over the midcheek skeleton, and describes age-related changes in discrete fat compartments.[1][2] Such papers describe anatomy for surgery and do not examine makeup.

card.summary: Shading and highlighting to imitate defined cheekbones; reversible and low-risk, with no clinical research behind it.
card.note: Effect is visual and depends on lighting and application.

quick.overview:
Cheekbone contouring uses darker and lighter makeup to suggest more defined cheekbones.

It is a styling technique and has not been studied clinically.
quick.mechanism: Shading under the cheekbone and highlighting on top change the perceived depth and shape of the cheek through light and shadow.
quick.risks: Makeup carries the usual risks of skin irritation or allergic reaction with some products. The effect is temporary and washes off.
